This threat intelligence product is specialized around recognizing an attacker’s thought process, eliminating pipelines and droppers, and is recognized as an evolving, cutting-edge technology within the industry.

TriVault has end-to-end solutions for every organization, and a price point that is yet to be beaten by any other professional cyber security firm due to low overhead and a conscientious decision made by all TriVault personnel to provide the best services. In an industry that is rapidly becoming bloated, stick with a partner you can trust in good times, and in bad, by reaching out to TriVault.

properties.name: MADDRIX
properties.description:
Maddrix is a professional services and technology company who's mission is to help the U.S. government, national security, critical infrastructure, and private sector organizations protect their trade secrets, mission critical programs, and national security information from targeted network attacks and nation state adversaries. We accomplish this by focusing on proactively identifying targeted network attacks and malware, and helping our clients with the paradigm shift from traditional perimeter and signature-based network defense programs to a comprehensive proactive model that addresses today’s advanced threat actors. 

Maddrix is in the inaugural class of only six incident response providers accredited by the National Security Agency under the National Security Cyber Assistance Program (NSCAP). To meet the eligibility requirements for this program, Maddrix was vetted against 21 critical focus areas of incident response. Part of this evaluation included a comprehensive review of our incident response and mitigation protocol, our ability to develop and maintain highly qualified incident response staff, and integrate lessons learned into our incident response protocol. 

We have developed a next generation advanced threat actor and malware detection solution called Endpoint Analytics (EA). Endpoint Analytics is an advanced analytics system that proactively detects targeted attacks and malware without known signatures. It works by collecting thousands of individual data points from each endpoint on the network, and subjecting those data points to big data analytics, enabling the rapid identification of active and non-active threat actor activity and malware. Endpoint Analytics scales to any size network, and is free for U.S. government agencies we support.

While there are numerous key points behind a successfully implemented security program, TriVault recognizes that the majority of threats from day-to-day activities happen on endpoints, which are commonly susceptible to vulnerabilities and malware. TriVault works to eradicate these threats from multiple angles through vulnerability management, patching, password management, EDR, threat intelligence, and all kinds of additional endpoint security platforms including data loss prevention.

Michael Mooney, the founder of TriVault, has engineered a threat intelligence platform that is designed as a dictionary reference of all sorts of different attack styles used by hackers. entity.description:
CYCON Security is a leading cybersecurity company specializing in automated Incident Response (IR) solutions and advanced cyber defense services.
Our flagship product, Hunter1 Platform, delivers a holistic and comprehensive view of cyberattacks — from initial access to full attack-chain visibility — enabling organizations to respond rapidly, accurately, and effectively.

Hunter1 Platform – Key Capabilities

1. Advanced Intelligence Gathering
Gain the attacker’s perspective.
Our platform continuously collects and analyzes data from the Dark Web, underground forums, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) to identify:
	•	Leaked credentials
	•	Exposed systems and assets
	•	Sensitive organizational data
— before it is weaponized by threat actors.

2. Endpoint & Server Investigation
Real-time anomaly detection across endpoints and servers uncovers suspicious behavior and unknown malicious code.
Hunter1 Platform pinpoints the origin of threats and delivers contextualized alerts with actionable insights for rapid decision-making.

3. Network Communication Analysis
Automated detection of suspicious inbound and outbound traffic across the organization’s infrastructure.
The platform identifies and blocks malicious communications using high-confidence indicators, including blacklisted or compromised IP addresses.

⸻

Core Areas of Expertise

Defensive Security:
	•	Incident Response (IR)
	•	Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI)
	•	Blue Team Operations
	•	Vulnerability Assessments
	•	Cybersecurity Training

Offensive & Preventive Security:
	•	Tactical Offensive Intelligence
	•	Red Team Simulations
	•	Application & Infrastructure Penetration Testing
	•	Threat Modeling
	•	Advanced CTI Analysis

Strategic Services:
	•	Regulatory Compliance & Risk Assessments
	•	Technology Evaluation & Proof of Concept (POC)
	•	Security Policy & Procedure Development
	•	Remediation Planning & Implementation

entity.name: MADDRIX
entity.description:
Maddrix is a professional services and technology company who's mission is to help the U.S. government, national security, critical infrastructure, and private sector organizations protect their trade secrets, mission critical programs, and national security information from targeted network attacks and nation state adversaries. We accomplish this by focusing on proactively identifying targeted network attacks and malware, and helping our clients with the paradigm shift from traditional perimeter and signature-based network defense programs to a comprehensive proactive model that addresses today’s advanced threat actors. 

Maddrix is in the inaugural class of only six incident response providers accredited by the National Security Agency under the National Security Cyber Assistance Program (NSCAP). To meet the eligibility requirements for this program, Maddrix was vetted against 21 critical focus areas of incident response. Part of this evaluation included a comprehensive review of our incident response and mitigation protocol, our ability to develop and maintain highly qualified incident response staff, and integrate lessons learned into our incident response protocol. 

We have developed a next generation advanced threat actor and malware detection solution called Endpoint Analytics (EA). Endpoint Analytics is an advanced analytics system that proactively detects targeted attacks and malware without known signatures. It works by collecting thousands of individual data points from each endpoint on the network, and subjecting those data points to big data analytics, enabling the rapid identification of active and non-active threat actor activity and malware. Endpoint Analytics scales to any size network, and is free for U.S. government agencies we support.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.
